run.tickTip: One tick is one simulated hour of company work
run.title: Runs the scheduled agents for the selected simulated time, in the background
pl.title: Plugins
pl.intro: Plugins extend corparius with extra providers, tools, templates and agents. Verified plugins come from the curated registry and are checked against a SHA-256.
pl.off: Plugins are off. Turn them on in Settings (Enable plugins), then restart.
pl.unverified: Installing an unverified plugin runs unaudited third-party code and is only possible from the command line, behind an explicit opt-in.
pl.regEmpty: The registry is empty for now.
sk.title: Skills
sk.intro: What this company knows, in prose. A skill is a SKILL.md folder under companies/<slug>/skills/ or the shared skills/ directory, read into the prompt when the tool about to run is one it names. Prose, not code: nothing here is executed.
sk.none: None written yet. Copy packaging/skill-template into companies/<slug>/skills/ to teach a company its own trade.
sk.off: Skills are off. Turn them on in Settings (Company skills).
sk.alwaysOn: {n} characters ride on every prompt of every agent, whatever the tool.
sk.scopeHelp: It costs {n} characters on every prompt of every agent. Tick the tools it is about, and it will only travel with those.
ob.title: Getting started
ob.desc: Three steps to a company working on its own. This card leaves once they are done.
ob.modelHint: Or stay in mock mode: it runs offline, free, deterministic. Real models live under Providers.
ob.runHint: Advance the clock a few hours and watch the agents work.
ob.decideHint: Money and production wait for you. Approve or reject the first one.
live.title: Go live
live.desc: Three things turn a simulated company into one that can take money: a checkout link, a mail account, and a public web address.
live.paidNo: button inert until you add a link
pulse.title: Company pulse
pulse.desc: Where the company stands right now. One tick is one simulated hour.
stat.hourTip: the company clock: one tick is one hour
progress.title: Progress
progress.desc: How much of the backlog is delivered.
activity.title: Recent activity
activity.desc: The last things agents did. Full log in Operations.
activity.empty: Nothing logged yet. Press Run above to simulate a few hours.
spend.title: Spend by agent
spend.empty: No spend yet. Run a day to see per-agent usage.
spend.noCost: Tokens only: none of the providers used report a cost. OpenRouter does.
flow.title: Flow
flow.desc: Is work flowing or piling up?
ops.waitingDesc: Money and production actions pause here until you decide. Nothing runs without you.
ops.calm: Nothing waits for a decision. The gate pauses money and production tools here.
ops.backlogDesc: The CEO's board. Proposals from agents need your call; the rest moves on its own.
ops.logEmpty: No actions logged for this company yet.
ops.whyGated: You named this tool in hitl_tools, so it always asks.
ops.rulesDesc: Tools you told the gate to stop asking about. Money and production tools cannot be listed here.
ops.rulesEmpty: No standing rule. Every gated tool still asks.
mem.title: What the company has learned
mem.desc: Facts its agents wrote down because they stay true. Pin one to keep it forever; forget one it got wrong.
mem.none: Nothing learned yet. The CEO and strategy agents write here as they run.
mem.off: Durable memory is off. Turn it on in Settings.
ib.question: asks you
ib.next.preflight: Press this and corparius calls each configured model for eight tokens, then tells you which ones your key can still use — and which tier to move.
ib.next.mail: This opens the Mail group of Settings, where the account is set up and tested for real.
ib.next.payments: This opens Settings, where the Stripe read key goes.
ib.next.plugins: This opens the Plugins tab, where one is enabled or installed.
ib.next.backlog: This opens the Backlog, where you set which agent and which tool should carry the task out — or reject it.
ib.next.providers: This opens the Providers tab, where a key is pasted and a tier is pointed at a model.
col.rest: {n} older ones stay in the store
prov.cloudHint: master gate for every remote provider
prov.ccHint: claudecode: target, subscription auth, no API credits
cc.mixed: Free providers keep the simple and everyday work ({n}); Opus takes the hard tier, and Sonnet backs the everyday work up once the free providers are exhausted.
cc.everyTier: No free provider is connected, so your subscription would serve every tier. Connect one in the list below to keep the simple work off your usage window.
cc.title: Use your Claude subscription
cc.desc: The simplest way to run on Claude: no API key, no credits, just your Claude Code login. One press sets everything up.
cc.readyNote: The tiers already route to your subscription.
cc.applying: Checking the CLI, then switching over…
cc.done: Done. Mock off, cloud on, and the tiers now run on your Claude subscription.
cc.desktop: Claude Desktop is installed on this machine, but that is the chat app. corparius drives the Claude Code CLI, a separate install on the same subscription — nothing more to buy.
cc.installed: CLI installed. Run `claude login` in a terminal once, then press Use your Claude subscription.
prov.serverFilled: Endpoint filled. Save it, then point a tier at custom:<model>.
oll.title: Local models (Ollama)
oll.desc: Free, offline, on your machine. corparius sees what is installed and pulls what your tiers need.
oll.measured: {c} cores, measured at {s} tokens/s on the {p}.
oll.stale: That measurement is old — measure again.
oll.unmeasured: Local speed not measured yet. Reachable is not capable: measure before giving a tier to local inference.
oll.serves: Local can serve the trivial tier —
oll.benching: Measuring — this runs one real generation and can take a minute.
oll.allSet: Every model your tiers need is installed.
prov.note: Changes apply to new calls immediately and are saved to the .env file. Mock mode serves every call from a deterministic offline mock.
prov.sweepConfirm: This calls {n} models across {p} providers, one real generation each. It uses your own keys and rate limits, and can take several minutes. Everything proved is kept even if you stop. Start?
prov.modelsHidden: ({n} hidden: proved not callable with this key)
prov.preflightRunning: Calling each one for eight tokens…
prov.pfSkippedWhy: Not an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so this cannot prove it.
prov.pfNothing: No tier points at an API provider, so there is nothing to call.
prov.freeNote: A provider joins the routing pool once its key is set (and cloud is enabled). Keys are write-only: the console never displays them back.
prov.ccNote: The claudecode target uses your local Claude Code CLI login instead of a key; enable it in Runtime.
prov.stillMock: Mock mode is on: saved keys are kept but not used yet. Turn mock off in Runtime.
prov.cloudOff: Cloud is disabled: saved keys are kept but not used yet. Enable cloud in Runtime.
prov.noCardTip: No payment card needed to sign up
prov.routingNote: Connected a free key? Let the console fill every tier coherently instead of typing model strings.
ceo.empty: Talk to the CEO agent about the plan, the backlog or the numbers. Replies use your configured routing (mock mode answers offline).
ceo.placeholder: Ask the CEO about the plan, the backlog, the numbers…
ceo.proposes: The CEO can do this now:
ceo.mockNote: Mock mode is on: the CEO echoes instead of thinking. Turn mock off and configure a provider in the Providers tab to talk to the real one.
ceo.name: CEO
ceo.role: The plan, the backlog, the numbers.
ceo.s2: How much have we taken in?
settings.title: Console settings
settings.desc: Stored in this browser only; they change nothing on the server.
site.title: Sales site
site.desc: The single-file page the design agent builds from the company config.
site.none: Not built yet. Generate it, then the design agent keeps it fresh.
pay.title: Payments
pay.desc: Money actually received, read from Stripe.
pay.mock: sample data: set STRIPE_API_KEY (restricted read key) for live payments
toast.routed: Routing set from your connected providers
wiz.title: Create your first company
wiz.desc: Two fields are enough to start. Everything else takes a sensible default and is editable under Settings.
wiz.name: Company name
wiz.productPh: Handmade scented candles, sold online in France.
wiz.hint: Runs offline in mock mode by default. Connect a free key in Providers, then Use recommended routing, to make it real.
diag.title: Diagnostics
diag.desc: Checks Python, the store, Ollama, providers and the network, and says what to fix.
up.confirm: Download the new build, check it against the published checksum and replace this program? Your companies and settings are in a separate folder and are not touched — a backup is taken first anyway.
up.done: corparius {v} is installed. Close this window and start corparius again to run it.
cfg.title: Configuration
cfg.desc: Everything corparius reads. Saved here, applied without touching a file. A field the process environment defines is shown read-only.
cfg.envTip: This value comes from the process environment, which outranks the console. Unset it in your shell or compose file to edit it here.
cfg.restartNote: Restart the console to apply it.
cfg.shadowedNote: Stored, but the environment still overrides: {keys}.
cfg.presetFilled: Hosts and ports filled. Add the address and an app password.
cfg.presetSendOnly: Sending host filled. This provider sends but has no mailbox to read.
cfg.advanced: Derived settings — filled from the provider, change only if needed
company.title: This company
company.desc: What the agents sell, to whom, and on what budget. Written straight to the company file.
company.name: Name
company.oneLinerHelp: The tagline on the sales site. Defaults to the product.
company.priceHelp: Shown on the sales site. Empty means no public price.
company.payLinkHelp: Where the site's button sends people. Falls back to the Stripe link in Configuration.
company.segmentHelp: Used as the lead search query and in site copy.
company.channelsHelp: The social agent posts to the first one.
company.painsHelp: Separated by | . Used on the site and as signal keywords.
company.tokensHelp: Overrides the global budget for this company.
company.hitlHelp: These tools never run until you decide.
company.rewrites: Saving rewrites that file from these fields. Comments you added by hand are not kept.
company.deleteHelp: Type {slug} to confirm. The config moves to companies/.trash and can be restored.
toast.loopStarted: Loop started. It runs in this console: close it and the loop stops.
site.headline: headline (optional, the agent writes one otherwise)
site.publishFailed: Nothing was published. Every provider failed:
site.publishNoProvider: Nothing was published: no provider is configured. Set one under Configuration, Publishing.
bk.title: Backup
bk.desc: Zips the store and every company config.
bk.warn: No API key leaves in plaintext: secrets are encrypted or blanked, and REDACTED.txt names what to re-enter. It still holds your companies and your journal, so keep it private.
dft.title: Written, not published
dft.desc: Posts the social agent wrote. Nothing in corparius publishes to a social channel, so they wait here. Copy one out, then mark it published so it stops counting.
dft.full: The queue is full, so the social agent has stopped writing until you clear some.
docs.title: What the company has on file
docs.desc: Files you dropped in, and files its agents wrote. Only what fits the prompt budget reaches a turn — anything past it is on disk and nothing reads it.
docs.none: Nothing on file yet. Drop a PDF, a deck, a spreadsheet or a note into the folder below and its text becomes context the agents can use.
docs.head: {n} on file · {r} reach the agents · {u} of {b} characters used
docs.more: {n} more on file, not listed here.
docs.no.no-such-document: {name} was not removed: it is not in the folder.
docs.no.outside: {name} was not removed: that path is not inside the folder.
docs.why.cut: reaches the agents: first {n} of {total} characters
docs.why.budget: on file, past the budget — no agent reads it
docs.why.image: sent as a picture, to a model that can read one
docs.why.no-text-layer: scanned or compressed: no text layer to read
docs.dropDesc: A pitch deck, a spec, a price list, a screenshot of a competitor's page. The text is extracted here on your machine and nothing is uploaded anywhere.
docs.accepts: Accepted: {list}. Up to {mb} MB per file.
docs.no.bad-name: {name} was not stored: that name would be written and then never read.
docs.no.no-extractor: {name} was not stored: nothing here can read {detail}, so it could never become context.
docs.no.empty-file: {name} was not stored: the file is empty.
docs.no.too-large: {name} was not stored: it is larger than the {mb} MB limit.
docs.no.write-failed: {name} was not stored: it could not be written. {detail}
token.needed: This console requires an access token.
footer: corparius operator console · serves on localhost · state is read from the local SQLite store
